title: Is Instinct safe to use? Three things to know before you sign up

reading.body:
Instinct is an AI personal assistant that collects and retains personal data from connected accounts without automatic deletion, even after users disconnect those accounts. The system can use this data to train AI models unless users find and enable opt-out settings. This represents a deployment without adequate defaults for user privacy, requiring users to affirmatively protect their own information rather than the system protecting it by default.

Instinct can make purchases on users' behalf using shared payment methods, with those transactions legally attributed to the user. If a purchase results in a dispute, users must resolve it directly with merchants rather than through Instinct. This is a system deployed to take consequential actions on behalf of users, with responsibility assigned to the user but without evidence of required user authorization for individual transactions.

It is not established whether these design choices resulted from negligence, intent, or standard industry practice, nor whether Instinct disclosed these behaviors in its terms of service or user interface.

reports.title: Is Instinct safe to use? Three things to know before you sign up

summary:
# Summary

Instinct is a new AI personal assistant gaining popularity in Silicon Valley, but it presents significant privacy and security risks that users should understand before adopting it. The application can use personal information to train AI models unless users actively opt out through specific settings. Additionally, Instinct collects data from connected accounts and retains that information even after users disconnect those accounts, meaning previous indexed data persists in Instinct's records without automatic deletion.

A third major concern is that Instinct can make purchases on users' behalf using shared payment methods, and these transactions are legally attributed to the user. If disputes arise, users must handle them directly with merchants rather than with Instinct. Norton argues that users should not sacrifice privacy and security for convenient AI assistance, promoting its own Norton Family Assistant as an alternative that keeps user data private and requires explicit consent before taking actions on behalf of users.
